title: Uber Builds MCP Gateway to Govern Access to 800+ Servers and 5,000+ AI Agent Tools
summary:
Uber has built an MCP Gateway to standardize how AI agents discover and invoke internal services across more than 800 MCP servers and 5,000 tools. The gateway separates tool registration from runtime execution and includes automated API discovery, access controls, sensitive data redaction, incremental tool discovery through Omni MCP, and response filtering.

By Leela Kumili

title: Vercel MCP now renders deployments as an interactive card
summary:

The card shows live deployment status, build logs, and source and commit details, with a Visit button once the deployment URL is ready. You can send logs into the chat to debug with the model, or open the fullscreen view to read them beneath the card. For repositories linked to multiple projects, a project list lets you switch between them.

The card is Vercel MCP's first MCP App, built on the MCP Apps extension. Clients without app support receive the deployment state, preview URL, and commit as text instead. title: Unslop Brings Staged UI Review to Claude Code and Codex
summary:
Unslop is a GitHub-hosted skill for Claude Code and Codex that targets what its author describes as “vibecoded, AI-looking” interfaces. For developers, the concrete change is an ordered review process: the skill audits a screen and proposes a design direction before it begins editing. The project documents the workflow and installation steps on GitHub.

From audit to ordered revisions

The audit identifies patterns including purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, forceful copy and uneven spacing. Unslop then derives a direction from the product, covering its character, visual world, limited uses of color and a signature detail. Its edits proceed through spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order. Those stages are specified in the project README.

title: I Built My Own Compiled Programming Language. Here's What I Learned.
summary:
Most developers use programming languages.

Some build applications with Python. Others use Rust, C, Go, or Java.

But at some point, I became interested in a different question:

What does it actually take to build a programming language?

Instead of just learning how existing languages work, I decided to build one myself.

That project became YLang.

Today, YLang is an open-source compiled programming language with its own compiler, documentation, development tools, and an evolving ecosystem.

This is the story of the project and what I have learned while developing it.

title: Add to calendar from the browser: generating .ics files for countdown dates
summary:
A countdown is more useful when it also lives in the calendar you already check every morning. An "Add to calendar" button is the simplest way to get it there, and you don't need a server or a library to build one. An .ics file is plain text, and the browser can create and download it on its own.

This tutorial builds that button step by step for an all-day countdown date like a wedding, a launch or a holiday. It also covers the details from RFC 5545 (the iCalendar spec) that are easy to get wrong.

The smallest valid file

An iCalendar file is a VCALENDAR that holds one or more VEVENTs. This is about as small as a valid one gets:

BEGIN:VCALENDAR
VERSION:2.0
PRODID:-//Example//Countdown//EN
CALSCALE:GREGORIAN
METHOD:PUBLISH
BEGIN:VEVENT
UID:3f9c2a1e-7b1d-4c55-9a0e-2d6f1b8e4c11@example.com
DTSTAMP:20261102T120000Z
DTSTART

title: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host
summary:
The fx adapter for the AI SDK’s HarnessAgent now uses libfx, the TypeScript library for fx. The harness and model requests run in your application’s process, while built-in filesystem and shell operations remain isolated in the sandbox.

This simplifies sandbox setup: you no longer need to install fx inside the sandbox, run a sandbox bridge, or expose a sandbox port. Model credentials stay on the host, outside the environment where the agent runs commands.

The rewrite also adds:

  • Built-in tool filtering: choose which built-in tools the agent can use

  • Mid-turn steering: send new instructions while a turn is running

  • Structured output: generate responses that match a schema

  • Image tool results: return images to the model through toModelOutput()

Sessions can be saved and resumed in a new host process.
